newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Danubius takes up loans of 75 mln marks.
newsitem.headline: Danubius takes up loans of 75 mln marks.

text.p: Hungarian hotel chain Danubius Rt took up loans totalling 75 million German marks from three banks to pay for its recent acquisition, the hotel company Hungaria Szalloda Rt, Danubius said on Monday in the Budapest Stock Exchange's (BSE) official gazette.
One of the loans, worth 25 million marks, has a maturity of one-year, while the other two loans, each of 25 million marks, have five-year maturities, Danubius said.

"The company has concluded each contracts with very favourable conditions, and the middle-term loans could be repaid any time ahead of maturity without extra cost," it added, without naming the lenders.
Danubius paid the purchasing price of Hungaria's 85 percent stake, sold by the state, from the loans to the state privatisation agency APV Rt on January 6, the company said.
Danubius bought the stake worth a nominal 4.675 billion forints, for 8.125 billion forints ($50 million) under an agreement signed on September 30 with APV.
The Competition Office cleared the deal in December, saying that the total market share of the merged hotel chains did not exceed the maximum permitted 30 percent.
Danubius closed at 4,300 forints, up 50, on the BSE on Monday.
